title: Token Slice Cost Journey + Pricing Pattern Library
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Design and prototype a set of token-level cost analytics screens and a small pricing UI pattern library for the Redwood Console. Goals: make per-route and per-customer token costs explorable, provide lineage/attribution of cost to prompts and model variants, and enable bulk export and publishing of pricing recommendations. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype (desktop), an interactive CSV/JSON export spec, a compact pricing pattern library (cards, toggles, attribution timeline), and a short handoff doc for engineering and PMs. This ticket covers research synthesis, wireframes, two prototype iterations, and a first round of cross-functional review with Eng and PM.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma prototype covers: route-level cost breakdown, token attribution timeline, model-variant cost comparison, and export flow
Design tokens/patterns documented for: compact cost cards, attribution flyouts, CSV/JSON export modal, and pricing suggestion banner
Design review notes addressed (accessibility contrast, mobile breakpoint behavior, and large-account CSV performance hints)
Engineering handoff includes component spec, data contract (fields required per export row), and sample dataset for QA
PM signs off on proposed pricing pattern copy and fallback states for missing telemetry
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha: Kickoff notes added. Initial research shows customers want per-route cost drift alerts and a simple CSV export for billing reconciliation.
2025-02-18 - Jonah: Wired up first low-fi flows. Decision: treat attribution as a first-class timeline view rather than embedding in the cost card to reduce cognitive load.
2025-02-21 - PM (Leah Chen): Asked for clarity on currency and billing granularity. Action: include late-binding currency conversion and an exported 'billing_unit' column.

2025-02-25 - Eng (Marco Rivera): Raised performance concern for computing token-attribution on-the-fly for large date ranges. Trade-off: show sampled attribution with 'full-export' option that runs an offline job.
2025-02-27 - Accessibility review (Nina Patel): Contrast issue on compact cost chips; updated color tokens to meet AA and added focus states for keyboard nav.
2025-03-01 - Jonah: Prototype 2 uploaded to Figma. Ready for design review and engineering estimation. Included sample export of 10k rows to validate CSV format.
2025-03-01 - Aisha: Added acceptance criteria and handoff checklist. Requesting review from PM and ENG for next Thursday sync.
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer progressive disclosure (cards -> timeline -> modal export) to avoid overwhelming new users
Export spec: include columns [timestamp, route, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, cost_usd, billing_unit, attribution_tags, request_id]
Pricing pattern idea: show 'suggested pricing band' card next to expensive routes with a one-click 'apply to plan' CTA that links to PM flow
Observability integration: add pointer to Console traces so users can jump from an expensive token spike to trace details (ENG dependency)
Performance note: for >50k rows export, offer server-side job + email link instead of immediate download
